answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the lantern schedule in the echo ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the dawn checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 219 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 1 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 9 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
